catalog.contract: Release the owned database handle. A completed SELECT has no implied result ordering without ORDER BY.

catalog.name: http_json

catalog.name: http_close
catalog.contract: Close the owned response. Function-scope cleanup also applies when reading or parsing fails.

contracts: The URL is supplied by the caller and identifies an HTTPS JSON API.
The timeout is a network-operation timeout, with the same interpretation as urllib timeout.
Response bodies and decoded JSON are fully materialized, so the response can be closed before returning.
HTTP, decoding and JSON errors propagate through the approved error contract after cleanup.

examples.title: C plus plus thread lifetime

catalog.name: worker_spawn
catalog.contract: Start the approved worker with an implicit cooperative stop token. Worker references 1 and 2 identify worker1 and worker2.

catalog.name: worker_join
catalog.contract: Wait for the owned worker to finish. On abnormal scope exit, remaining owned workers receive stop requests and are joined.

contracts: The source requires C++20 std::jthread. Approved worker bodies are supplied elsewhere.
Workers accept a stop token, cooperate with cancellation and handle/report their own exceptions without allowing exceptions to escape.
The normal path joins both workers. Completion order is unrestricted.
A failed second spawn triggers stop/join cleanup of the first owned worker, corresponding to jthread scope cleanup.
The native runtime scheduling policy and performance remain separate implementation choices.

examples.title: Ruby paid order totals
examples.source:
def paid_totals(orders)
  totals = Hash.new(0)
  orders.each do |order|
    next unless order[:paid]
    totals[order[:customer]] += order[:amount_cents]
  end
  totals.sort.to_h
end

catalog.name: rows_where_true
catalog.contract: Keep rows whose declared boolean field is true.

catalog.name: sum_by_key
catalog.contract: Sum exact integer cent amounts for each customer, starting at zero.

catalog.name: sort_group_keys
catalog.contract: Return the mapping with ascending ASCII string keys.

contracts: Every row has a boolean paid value, an ASCII customer string and an exact integer amount_cents.
Amounts use integer cents, including negative refunds. Addition uses exact integer semantics.
Output preserves ascending customer-key iteration order.
The approved filter, grouping and sorting implementations contain the traversal loops.

examples.title: Java active user emails

catalog.name: active_rows
catalog.contract: Keep rows whose declared boolean field is true.

catalog.name: project_field
catalog.contract: Read the required non-null email field from each selected row.

catalog.name: distinct_values
catalog.contract: Keep one occurrence of each exact string value.

catalog.name: sort_strings
catalog.contract: Return unique email values sorted by Java String natural order. The example fixture domain is ASCII.

contracts: The source targets Java 17 or later and uses record, streams and Stream.toList.
Every input User has a boolean active flag and a non-null ASCII email string.
Equality and ordering are case-sensitive. ASCII restriction gives the mock oracle the same ordering as Java String natural order.
The returned email sequence is immutable, matching the Stream.toList result contract.
